items.definition: The Incoterms rules, published by the International Chamber of Commerce, are eleven three-letter trade terms that say, for a sale of goods, where the seller delivers, where risk passes to the buyer, which costs each side pays and who does export and import clearance. The current edition is Incoterms 2020.
items.definition_ar: قواعد الإنكوترمز الصادرة عن غرفة التجارة الدولية هي إحدى عشرة قاعدة من ثلاثة أحرف تحدد في عقد البيع مكان تسليم البائع، ونقطة انتقال المخاطر للمشتري، والتكاليف على كل طرف، ومن يتولى تخليص التصدير والاستيراد. الإصدار الحالي هو إنكوترمز 2020.
items.explanation: Seven rules are for any mode (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP) and four for sea and inland waterway only (FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF). Write the rule with a precise named place and the edition, e.g. 'FCA Antwerp terminal Incoterms 2020'. The C rules have two critical points: the seller pays carriage to destination, but risk passes at shipment. The rules do not decide when ownership passes, the price or payment, or what happens on breach — the sale contract does.
misconceptions: Incoterms are not law; they apply because the contract says so.
Incoterms do not say when ownership (title) passes.
Under CIF the seller pays freight to destination, but the buyer carries the risk during the voyage.
limitations: ATLAS describes the rules in its own words; the ICC text is the authority and the contract can vary a rule.

items.definition: Under EXW the seller delivers by placing the goods at the buyer's disposal at the seller's premises (or another named place), not loaded and not cleared for export. The buyer bears all costs and risks from there.
items.definition_ar: في EXW يسلم البائع بوضع البضاعة تحت تصرف المشتري في مقره أو مكان مسمى، دون تحميل ودون تخليص تصدير، ويتحمل المشتري كل التكاليف والمخاطر من تلك النقطة.
items.explanation: EXW puts the most obligation on the buyer, including export clearance in the seller's country, which a foreign buyer may not be able to do legally. FCA is often the better choice when the buyer arranges transport.

synonyms: containers handed over at a terminal
items.definition: Under FCA the seller, cleared for export, delivers the goods to the carrier or person nominated by the buyer at the named place; risk passes there. If the named place is the seller's premises, the seller loads the buyer's vehicle; elsewhere, delivery is on the seller's vehicle ready for unloading.
items.definition_ar: في FCA يسلم البائع البضاعة مخلصة للتصدير إلى الناقل الذي يحدده المشتري في المكان المسمى وتنتقل المخاطر هناك؛ إذا كان المكان مقر البائع فالبائع يحمّل وسيلة المشتري، وإلا فالتسليم على وسيلة البائع جاهزة للتفريغ.
items.explanation: FCA is the ICC's recommended rule for containerised cargo handed over at a terminal, where FOB does not fit. Incoterms 2020 lets the parties agree that the buyer's carrier issues an on-board bill of lading to the seller, which letters of credit often require.

items.definition: Under CPT the seller contracts and pays carriage to the named destination, but risk passes to the buyer when the goods are handed to the first carrier. The seller clears for export; the buyer clears for import.
items.definition_ar: في CPT يتعاقد البائع ويدفع أجرة النقل حتى الوجهة المسماة، لكن المخاطر تنتقل للمشتري عند تسليم البضاعة لأول ناقل. البائع يخلص التصدير والمشتري يخلص الاستيراد.

items.definition: CIP is CPT plus insurance: the seller pays carriage to the named destination and insures the goods for the buyer, while risk still passes when the goods are handed to the first carrier.
items.definition_ar: CIP هي CPT مضافًا إليها التأمين: يدفع البائع النقل حتى الوجهة ويؤمّن البضاعة لصالح المشتري، مع انتقال المخاطر عند التسليم لأول ناقل.
items.explanation: Incoterms 2020 raised CIP's minimum cover to all-risks level (Institute Cargo Clauses (A)), unlike CIF, whose minimum stays at Clauses (C).

items.definition: Under DAP the seller bears costs and risks to the named place of destination and delivers the goods there on the arriving means of transport, ready for unloading. The buyer unloads and clears for import, paying duties.
items.definition_ar: في DAP يتحمل البائع التكاليف والمخاطر حتى مكان الوجهة المسمى ويسلم البضاعة على وسيلة النقل الواصلة جاهزة للتفريغ، ويتولى المشتري التفريغ وتخليص الاستيراد ودفع الرسوم.
items.explanation: Demurrage caused by the buyer's slow import clearance is usually the buyer's under DAP, because clearance is the buyer's job — check the contract.

items.definition: Under DPU the seller delivers once the goods are unloaded at the named place of destination; it is the only rule where the seller unloads at destination. The buyer clears for import. DPU replaced DAT in Incoterms 2020.
items.definition_ar: في DPU يكتمل تسليم البائع بعد تفريغ البضاعة في مكان الوجهة المسمى، وهي القاعدة الوحيدة التي يفرغ فيها البائع في الوجهة. المشتري يخلص الاستيراد. حلت DPU محل DAT في إنكوترمز 2020.

items.definition: Under DDP the seller delivers at the named destination cleared for import with duties and taxes paid, ready for unloading — the maximum obligation for the seller.
items.definition_ar: في DDP يسلم البائع البضاعة في الوجهة المسماة مخلصة للاستيراد ومدفوعة الرسوم والضرائب جاهزة للتفريغ، وهو أقصى التزام على البائع.
items.explanation: The seller must be able to act as importer (or use an agent who can) in the buyer's country, and some import taxes may not be recoverable by a foreign seller. Many countries' rules make DDP impractical for foreign sellers.

items.definition: Under FAS (sea and inland waterway only) the seller delivers when the goods are placed alongside the buyer's vessel at the named port of shipment, cleared for export; risk passes there.
items.definition_ar: في FAS (للنقل البحري والنهري فقط) يسلم البائع بوضع البضاعة بجانب سفينة المشتري في ميناء الشحن المسمى مخلصة للتصدير، وتنتقل المخاطر هناك.

items.definition: Under FOB (sea and inland waterway only) the seller, cleared for export, delivers the goods on board the vessel nominated by the buyer at the named port of shipment; risk passes once they are on board. The buyer contracts and pays the main carriage.
items.definition_ar: في FOB (للبحري والنهري فقط) يسلم البائع البضاعة مخلصة للتصدير على ظهر السفينة التي يحددها المشتري في ميناء الشحن المسمى، وتنتقل المخاطر بمجرد التحميل على السفينة، ويتعاقد المشتري على النقل الرئيسي ويدفعه.
items.explanation: For containers the seller normally hands the box to the terminal days before loading, so under FOB it carries risk for goods it no longer controls; the ICC advises FCA for containerised goods. FOB is also used informally for air freight, but that is not an Incoterms use.
misconceptions: FOB is not an 'any mode' rule: using it for air cargo is outside the Incoterms rules.
Under FOB the buyer, not the seller, books the ocean freight.

items.definition: Under CFR (sea and inland waterway only) the seller contracts and pays carriage to the named port of destination, but risk passes to the buyer when the goods are on board the vessel at the port of shipment.
items.definition_ar: في CFR (للبحري والنهري فقط) يتعاقد البائع ويدفع النقل حتى ميناء الوجهة المسمى، لكن المخاطر تنتقل للمشتري عند تحميل البضاعة على السفينة في ميناء الشحن.

items.definition: CIF is CFR plus insurance: the seller pays carriage to the named port of destination and insures the goods for the buyer (minimum Institute Cargo Clauses (C)), while risk passes once the goods are on board at the port of shipment. Sea and inland waterway only.
items.definition_ar: CIF هي CFR مضافًا إليها التأمين: يدفع البائع النقل حتى ميناء الوجهة ويؤمّن البضاعة لصالح المشتري (حد أدنى شروط المجمع (C))، بينما تنتقل المخاطر عند التحميل في ميناء الشحن. للبحري والنهري فقط.
items.explanation: 'CIF value' is also used in customs: many countries assess import duty on the cost of the goods plus insurance and freight to the border, whatever Incoterms rule the sale used. That is a customs valuation rule, separate from the trade term — see customs valuation.
misconceptions: Paying the freight under CIF does not mean the seller carries the risk during the voyage.

items.definition: The commercial invoice is the seller's bill for the goods: seller and buyer, description, quantities, unit and total prices, currency, Incoterms rule and payment terms. Customs uses it as the starting point for valuation.
items.definition_ar: الفاتورة التجارية هي فاتورة البائع للبضاعة: البائع والمشتري والوصف والكميات وأسعار الوحدة والإجمالي والعملة وقاعدة الإنكوترمز وشروط الدفع، وتعتمد عليها الجمارك كبداية للتقييم.
items.explanation: Mismatches between the invoice, packing list and transport document (quantities, weights, descriptions, consignee) are among the most frequent causes of customs holds. A proforma invoice is a quotation or advance invoice and is usually not accepted for clearance on its own.

items.definition: The packing list shows how the goods are packed: packages, marks and numbers, contents of each package, net and gross weights and dimensions.
items.definition_ar: قائمة التعبئة توضح طريقة تعبئة البضاعة: عدد الطرود وعلاماتها وأرقامها ومحتوى كل طرد والأوزان الصافية والإجمالية والأبعاد.
items.explanation: Customs uses it to plan inspections and match packages; the carrier's piece count and weight should agree with it.

items.definition: A bill of lading (B/L) is the document a sea carrier issues for a shipment: a receipt for the cargo, evidence of the contract of carriage and, when negotiable, title to the goods.
items.definition_ar: بوليصة الشحن (B/L) مستند يصدره الناقل البحري للشحنة: إيصال باستلام البضاعة ودليل على عقد النقل، وعندما تكون قابلة للتداول فهي سند ملكية للبضاعة.
items.explanation: Its number is the reference used to track an ocean shipment with the carrier. A negotiable ('to order') original must be surrendered to take delivery; a telex release or sea waybill lets the consignee collect without originals. The line's master B/L and a forwarder's or NVOCC's house B/L can both exist for one shipment.

items.definition: A sea waybill is a non-negotiable transport document: the named consignee can take delivery without presenting an original. A telex (express) release is the carrier's instruction that the originals were surrendered at origin, so delivery may be made without them at destination.
items.definition_ar: بوليصة Sea waybill مستند نقل غير قابل للتداول يسمح للمرسل إليه المسمى بالاستلام دون أصل. والإفراج بالتلكس تعليمات من الناقل بأن الأصول سُلمت في المنشأ فيمكن التسليم في الوجهة بدونها.
items.explanation: Waiting for couriered original B/Ls is a classic cause of demurrage; waybills and telex releases avoid it when no bank needs to control the goods.

items.definition: An air waybill (AWB) is the transport document for air cargo. Its 11-digit number starts with the airline's 3-digit prefix (for example 057 for Air France, 074 for KLM, 157 for Qatar Airways), which is how the automation knows which airline to ask.
items.definition_ar: بوليصة الشحن الجوي (AWB) مستند نقل البضائع جوًا. يبدأ رقمها المكون من 11 خانة ببادئة الشركة المكونة من 3 أرقام (مثل 057 لإير فرانس و074 لـ KLM و157 للقطرية)، وبها تعرف الأتمتة أي شركة تسأل.
items.explanation: An AWB is not negotiable and is not a document of title. A forwarder's house AWB (HAWB) sits under the airline's master AWB (MAWB); the airline tracks the master number. IATA promotes the electronic AWB (e-AWB).

sources.note: Migrated from ATLAS's glossary; the airline prefixes are the ones update_eta.py uses.

items.definition: A certificate of origin states the country where the goods were produced, as defined by rules of origin. A preferential certificate can reduce duty under a trade agreement.
items.definition_ar: شهادة المنشأ تثبت البلد الذي أُنتجت فيه البضاعة وفق قواعد المنشأ، والشهادة التفضيلية قد تخفض الرسوم بموجب اتفاقية تجارية.
items.explanation: Origin is where the goods were made or last substantially transformed, not where they were shipped from. Preferential rates need the agreement's own proof of origin, issued correctly; a missing or wrong certificate usually means paying the full rate.
misconceptions: Country of origin is not the country of shipment.

items.full_form: Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System
items.definition: HS classification assigns goods a code in the WCO's Harmonized System: 6 digits shared internationally, extended by each country to 8–10 digits for its tariff. The code decides the duty rate and which import controls apply.
items.definition_ar: التصنيف الجمركي يعطي البضاعة رمزًا في النظام المنسق لمنظمة الجمارك العالمية: 6 أرقام دولية، تمددها كل دولة إلى 8-10 أرقام في تعريفتها، ويحدد الرمز نسبة الرسوم والضوابط المطبقة.
items.explanation: Classification follows the General Interpretative Rules, starting with the heading texts and section and chapter notes. The HS is amended about every five years (the HS 2022 edition is in force since 1 January 2022), and countries move to new editions on their own timetable, so the national tariff is the authority for a code.
items.example: A spare engine for an excavator and a complete excavator fall under different headings and may carry different duty rates.

items.definition: A customs declaration is the formal statement to customs of the goods, their classification, value, origin and the procedure requested (import for home use, transit, warehousing, temporary admission, export).
items.definition_ar: الإقرار الجمركي هو البيان الرسمي للجمارك عن البضاعة وتصنيفها وقيمتها ومنشئها والإجراء المطلوب (استيراد للاستهلاك، ترانزيت، تخزين، إدخال مؤقت، تصدير).
items.explanation: The declarant is legally responsible for its accuracy; errors lead to amendments, penalties or holds. National systems differ (Ghana's ICUMS, Egypt's Nafeza single window).

items.definition: A Bill of Entry is the customs declaration for imported goods: it lists the goods, their value, and the duties and taxes assessed.
items.definition_ar: بيان الاستيراد (Bill of Entry) هو الإقرار الجمركي للبضائع المستوردة ويذكر البضائع وقيمتها والرسوم والضرائب المقدرة.
items.explanation: The PO automation reads the Bill of Entry attached to an Under Clearance record in eHub to calculate and prepare the duty PO.

items.definition: Import duties and taxes are what the importing country charges on goods: customs duty set by the tariff for the HS code and origin, plus import VAT or sales tax and other national levies, calculated on the customs value.
items.definition_ar: الرسوم والضرائب الجمركية ما تفرضه دولة الاستيراد على البضائع: رسم جمركي حسب البند الجمركي والمنشأ، وضريبة القيمة المضافة على الواردات ورسوم وطنية أخرى، محسوبة على القيمة الجمركية.
items.explanation: Rates and levies are national and change with each budget; ATLAS does not state a country's rates from memory. The PO automation computes duty only from the figures on the Bill of Entry itself.

items.definition: Customs valuation determines the value duty is charged on. Under the WTO Valuation Agreement the primary method is the transaction value — the price actually paid or payable — with set additions and deductions; five fallback methods apply when it cannot be used.
items.definition_ar: التقييم الجمركي يحدد القيمة التي تُحسب عليها الرسوم. وفق اتفاقية التقييم في منظمة التجارة العالمية فالطريقة الأساسية هي قيمة الصفقة (السعر المدفوع فعلًا أو المستحق) مع إضافات وخصومات محددة، وتوجد خمس طرق بديلة عند تعذرها.
items.explanation: Whether freight and insurance to the border are included (a CIF basis) or not (an FOB basis) is a national choice, so the same goods can have a different customs value in different countries regardless of the Incoterms rule of the sale.

items.term: Ghana: duty on the CIF value
items.definition: In Ghana, import duty is assessed on the CIF value of the goods (cost, insurance and freight to the port of entry).
items.definition_ar: في غانا تُحسب رسوم الاستيراد على قيمة CIF للبضاعة (التكلفة والتأمين والشحن حتى ميناء الدخول).
items.explanation: This was stated in ATLAS's original glossary. It has not yet been checked against a Ghana Revenue Authority publication, so it is marked unverified until a reviewer confirms it against GRA's current rules.
limitations: Unverified. Check the current GRA Customs rules before relying on it.

sources.note: The authority to verify against; not quoted.

items.definition: Egypt requires shipment data to be registered in advance through the Nafeza single window (the ACI system), producing an ACID number that must appear on the shipping documents of sea imports.
items.definition_ar: تشترط مصر تسجيل بيانات الشحنات مسبقًا عبر منصة نافذة (نظام ACI) للحصول على رقم ACID يجب أن يظهر في مستندات الشحن للواردات البحرية.
items.explanation: Scope, dates and the treatment of air freight have changed over time; this item states the general requirement only and is unverified until a reviewer checks it against Nafeza's current rules.
limitations: Unverified; scope by mode and the effective dates must be checked on Nafeza.

items.definition: Customs clearance is getting goods through customs: lodging the declaration with its documents, classification and valuation, risk assessment and any inspection, payment of duties and taxes, and release.
items.definition_ar: التخليص الجمركي هو إنهاء إجراءات الجمارك: تقديم الإقرار ومستنداته، والتصنيف والتقييم، وتقييم المخاطر والتفتيش إن وجد، وسداد الرسوم والضرائب، ثم الإفراج.
items.explanation: Other agencies (standards, health, agriculture) may need permits before customs releases the goods. Every day spent in clearance consumes the port's and carrier's free time, so slow clearance turns into demurrage and storage charges. In eHub, Under Clearance is the shipment status for this stage.

items.definition: A customs hold is customs stopping the release of goods until something is resolved: a document, an inspection, a valuation or classification query, an unpaid amount, another agency's permit, or an enforcement concern.
items.definition_ar: الحجز الجمركي هو إيقاف الجمارك للإفراج عن البضاعة حتى حل أمر ما: مستند، أو تفتيش، أو استفسار عن التقييم أو التصنيف، أو مبلغ غير مدفوع، أو تصريح جهة أخرى، أو اشتباه رقابي.
items.explanation: The first step is to find out which of these it is — from the customs system, the broker or the carrier — before acting. A DHL 'Shipment is on hold' with a 'Clearance Event' at destination means the destination clearance is stopped, not that the shipment is lost.

items.definition: Customs risk-assesses each declaration and routes it: release without checks (often 'green'), a documentary check ('yellow'), or a physical examination or scan ('red'). Channel names and colours vary by country.
items.definition_ar: تقيّم الجمارك مخاطر كل إقرار وتوجهه: إفراج دون فحص (الأخضر غالبًا)، أو فحص مستندي (الأصفر)، أو معاينة فعلية أو أشعة (الأحمر). تختلف التسميات والألوان من دولة لأخرى.
items.explanation: A physical examination adds days: scheduling, unstuffing the container, and any queries it raises. Consistent, accurate declarations lower the chance of selection over time in risk-based systems.

sources.note: Risk management is one of the TFA's measures; channel names are national.

items.definition: A documentation discrepancy is a difference between documents for the same shipment — invoice, packing list, transport document, certificate of origin, manifest, declaration — or a missing required document.
items.definition_ar: تعارض المستندات هو اختلاف بين مستندات الشحنة الواحدة (الفاتورة وقائمة التعبئة ومستند النقل وشهادة المنشأ والمانيفست والإقرار) أو غياب مستند مطلوب.
items.explanation: Typical ones: quantity or weight differs between invoice and B/L; consignee name differs from the importer's registration; the HS code in the declaration does not match the description. Fixing them may need an amendment from the shipper or carrier, which takes time — hence holds and demurrage.

items.definition: Release is customs allowing the goods to leave customs control for the procedure declared — usually after duties are paid or guaranteed and checks are complete.
items.definition_ar: الإفراج هو سماح الجمارك بخروج البضاعة من رقابتها وفق الإجراء المعلن، عادة بعد سداد الرسوم أو ضمانها واكتمال الفحوص.
items.explanation: Customs release is not the end: the terminal still needs the carrier's delivery order and its own charges paid before the container can leave.

items.definition: Demurrage is the charge for leaving a container inside the port/terminal beyond the free days allowed.
items.definition_ar: الديمراج هو رسم بقاء الحاوية داخل الميناء أو المحطة بعد انتهاء أيام السماح.
items.explanation: It is different from detention, which is charged for keeping the carrier's container outside the terminal (at your premises) beyond its free time. Delays in customs clearance are a common cause of demurrage. Some carriers combine both into one 'D&D' free-time allowance.

items.definition: Detention is the charge for keeping the carrier's container outside the terminal beyond the free time — for example while it is being unloaded at your warehouse.
items.definition_ar: غرامة الاحتجاز (Detention) هي رسم الاحتفاظ بحاوية الناقل خارج المحطة بعد انتهاء فترة السماح، مثلًا أثناء تفريغها في مخزنك.
items.explanation: Demurrage is the equivalent charge while the container is still in the port. The detention clock usually stops when the empty container is returned to the depot the carrier names.

items.definition: Free time is the number of days the carrier or terminal allows before demurrage or detention charges start.
items.definition_ar: فترة السماح هي عدد الأيام التي يسمح بها الناقل أو المحطة قبل بدء رسوم الديمراج أو الاحتجاز.
items.explanation: Free time is set by the carrier's tariff or the customer's contract, and terminal storage has its own free period. Knowing the last free day is the basis for prioritising which clearances to push first.

items.definition: Storage charges are what the terminal, port or warehouse operator bills for keeping cargo beyond its own free period. They are separate from the carrier's demurrage and can run at the same time.
items.definition_ar: رسوم التخزين (الأرضيات) يفرضها مشغل المحطة أو الميناء أو المخزن عن بقاء البضاعة بعد فترة سماحه، وهي منفصلة عن ديمراج الناقل وقد تُحتسب في نفس الوقت.

items.definition: The manifest is the carrier's list of all cargo on a vessel or flight, filed with customs before arrival so the goods can be declared and cleared.
items.definition_ar: المانيفست قائمة الناقل بكل البضائع على السفينة أو الطائرة، تُقدم للجمارك قبل الوصول ليمكن الإقرار عنها وتخليصها.
items.explanation: A shipment 'manifested onto' a flight is planned on it, not proven to have departed: only a departure event says it left.

items.definition: Dangerous goods are articles or substances that can endanger health, safety or property in transport (flammable, corrosive, toxic, lithium batteries, compressed gases). They must be classified, packed, marked, labelled and declared under the rules of each mode — IATA DGR for air, the IMDG Code for sea.
items.definition_ar: البضائع الخطرة مواد أو أصناف قد تهدد الصحة أو السلامة أو الممتلكات أثناء النقل (قابلة للاشتعال، أكالة، سامة، بطاريات ليثيوم، غازات مضغوطة)، ويجب تصنيفها وتعبئتها ووسمها والإقرار عنها وفق قواعد كل وسيلة: لوائح IATA للجوي ومدونة IMDG للبحري.
items.explanation: Spare parts can be DG without looking dangerous (batteries, some lubricants, aerosols, fire suppression cylinders). Undeclared DG is refused, delayed or fined. The IATA DGR is reissued yearly.

items.definition: A single window lets traders lodge all import, export and transit information once, through one entry point, to all the agencies that need it.
items.definition_ar: النافذة الواحدة تتيح للتجار تقديم كل بيانات الاستيراد والتصدير والترانزيت مرة واحدة عبر نقطة دخول واحدة لكل الجهات المعنية.
items.explanation: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement encourages members to establish one. Examples in Mantrac's countries include Egypt's Nafeza and Ghana's ICUMS.

items.term: House and master bill of lading
items.definition: A master bill of lading is issued by the ocean carrier to the forwarder or NVOCC; a house bill of lading is issued by that forwarder to the actual shipper for its goods inside the shipment.
items.explanation: The consignee's release at destination depends on the house B/L being surrendered to the forwarder, and the forwarder's on the master B/L to the carrier. A 'released' master does not mean the house has been released.

items.definition: A letter of credit (documentary credit) is a bank's undertaking to pay the seller when the seller presents documents that comply exactly with the credit's terms.
items.explanation: Banks check documents, not goods: a small discrepancy — a date, a weight, a description that differs from the credit — can block payment. Shipping documents for an LC shipment must match the credit word for word.
limitations: The rules that usually govern credits (ICC's UCP) are a paid publication and are not quoted here.

items.definition: An arrival notice is the carrier's or forwarder's notice to the consignee or notify party that a shipment is arriving or has arrived, with charges due and what is needed for release.
items.explanation: It starts the practical clock: free time often begins at discharge, so acting late on the arrival notice turns into demurrage.

items.definition: Pre-arrival processing is lodging import documents and data with customs before the goods arrive, so customs can begin processing and release can follow quickly on arrival.
items.explanation: The WTO Trade Facilitation Agreement requires members to allow it (Article 7.1). Sending documents late to the broker removes this advantage and is a frequent cause of clearance delay.

items.term: Customs risk management and inspection channels
items.definition: Customs risk management is customs deciding which consignments to check, and how closely, from risk criteria instead of checking everything; many administrations route declarations to channels such as documentary check or physical inspection.
items.explanation: The WTO TFA requires members, to the extent possible, to maintain a risk-management system for customs control (Article 7.4). A declaration sent for physical inspection is not an accusation; it adds time, so plan for it on new suppliers, new HS codes or high-value goods.
limitations: The channel names and criteria are national; ATLAS does not know a given country's.

items.definition: A post-clearance audit is customs checking declarations, records and payments after the goods have been released, to verify compliance.
items.explanation: Release is not the end: customs can later reassess value, classification or origin and claim more duty. Keep the commercial and shipping documents. The WTO TFA requires members to maintain post-clearance audit (Article 7.5).

items.definition: An authorized economic operator (AEO) is a trader recognised by customs as meeting compliance and security criteria, in return for facilitation such as fewer inspections or faster release.
items.explanation: The WCO SAFE Framework introduced the AEO programme; the WTO TFA requires members to offer additional facilitation to operators who meet specified criteria (Article 7.7). The benefits and criteria are national.

items.definition: Release before final determination lets customs release goods before the final amount of duties and taxes is decided, usually against a guarantee or deposit.
items.explanation: Useful when a valuation or classification question would otherwise hold the goods. The WTO TFA requires members to allow it where the final amount is not determined at or before arrival, subject to conditions (Article 7.3).

items.definition: Temporary admission lets goods enter a customs territory for a specific purpose and period with duties and taxes conditionally relieved, provided they are re-exported in the same state.
items.explanation: Typical uses: equipment for a project or demonstration, tools, goods for repair. The WTO TFA requires members to allow it as provided in their laws (Article 10.9). The conditions, guarantees and periods are national.
limitations: Whether a specific item qualifies, the guarantee required and the period allowed depend on the importing country.

items.definition: Expedited shipment procedures let customs release goods entered through air cargo facilities by express operators quickly, with simplified documentation, while keeping customs control.
items.explanation: The WTO TFA requires members to maintain such procedures for at least air cargo (Article 7.8). Express couriers clear many small shipments this way, which is why a DHL Express parcel and a forwarder's air consolidation clear differently.

items.definition: Duty drawback is the refund of import duties paid on goods that are later exported, or used to make goods that are exported, under the conditions a country sets.
items.explanation: It needs records linking the import to the export. Whether drawback exists, and on what, is national law.
limitations: A national scheme; ATLAS does not state any country's conditions.
